Party: Patrol Partners.description:
🏃 A sidekick, a vigilante and some locals chase the same thief through an arcade full of All Might figures.

📍 The hero merch arcade · Sunday evening
🎭 Group start: partnerships have begun in stranger ways
👥 For Sidekicks, Pro Heroes, Vigilantes and Civilian Life together
Party: Patrol Partners.storyStart:
THE SITUATION: It is Sunday evening, the weekend U.A. Academy's first-years moved into their dorms and the week All Might begins teaching there. You and several other player characters are in the Hero Merch Arcade off Musutafu Station's south exit for reasons of your own: a licensed sidekick on an agency's foot patrol, a vigilante keeping watch on the station blocks without a license, a part-timer restocking a shop, a collector, or a commuter cutting through. Your Backgrounds decide who you are and whether you know each other; if silent, you are strangers. A licensed sidekick may act on duty under their agency; anyone else who uses a Quirk in public outside self-defense breaks the law, even to help.
THE PLACE: The Hero Merch Arcade: a bright covered shopping street lined with narrow shops selling hero figures, trading cards, posters, replica costumes, signed photos, and fan magazines. Golden All Might goods fill the front shelves of every store; Endeavor, Best Jeanist, and Hawks have their own flashy displays, and Mount Lady merchandise sells fast. Plastic capsule-toy machines rattle, the air smells of vinyl and sweet station crepes, and every shop speaker blasts a different hero-news clip. Collectors and commuters pack the walkway; one end opens on the Station Concourse, the other on the dim Back Alleys.
THE MOMENT: A shop owner's desperate shout—Mrs. Ueda's—cuts through the bustle: a young man with a slippery Quirk, Yuto Kubo, has swept a glass case of signed All Might cards into a bag and is sprinting for the Back Alleys, shoving through the crowd. A capsule machine topples with a crash and scatters plastic spheres across the tile walkway. Show each of you (each PC) in the arcade with one vivid detail at the exact moment the thief bolts past you.
WHO MAY APPEAR:
- Kamui Woods: a focused capture specialist from Hero Agency Row who patrols the station blocks and binds suspects in one move; calm and sparing with words.
- Mount Lady: a flashy rookie with her own shelf in the arcade; the covered walkway is too low for her giant form, which she hates, and she poses for any phone.
- Death Arms: a burly frontline street pro who charges in shouting booming warnings.
- Backdraft: a steady rescue pro who handles any fire or collapse and always counts heads first.
- Sansa Tamakawa: the police officer who takes statements on Quirk incidents, called in once the police box reports.
The thief, the shop owner, and the fans are generated people. A pro arrives only after real time passes, unless a PC's agency is already on the radio.
OPENING HOOKS:
- Licensed Pro Hero: you run a small agency and are off duty, hunting for a niece's birthday gift, when the thief barrels past.
- Licensed Sidekick: you are on foot patrol and the radio is already asking for your position; procedure says report, secure the crowd, and pursue within your license.
- Vigilante: you know the Back Alleys better than any patrol and could cut the thief off, at the cost of using a Quirk right in front of a licensed sidekick.
- Civilian Life: you work at the robbed shop, and the owner, Mrs. Ueda, is already fretting that the loss will come out of someone's pay.
- Police Family: you know what a clean statement and a witness description do for a case, and what they can do to a vigilante.
- Hero Family: a parent's smiling face is on a poster above the walkway, and the shop owner recognizes you from family photos.
- Default: the thief's shoulder clips you as he races past, and something tumbles out of his bag right at your feet.
RULES:
- The opening stays in the Hero Merch Arcade; the Back Alleys and the Station Concourse are separate areas.
- Each PC's Quirk works exactly as your traits state; a hero license covers only its holder, and only on duty.
- Each player acts and answers for themselves; nobody leads unless you choose, and no choice binds another PC.
- No canon event happens or is foretold here; pros arrive only after real time passes.
- End on the open, breathless moment, the thief running and the crowd in the way.

THE FIRST DAYS (background for later turns; the opening stays on THE MOMENT):
- A sidekick's days run through their agency: patrol shifts, radio check-ins, a report after every incident, and arguments over case credit.
- A vigilante's run the other way: a daytime life, tense nights in the Back Alleys, no radio, and no backup.
- Civilians keep their shifts in the arcade or commute through the Station Concourse; their Quirks stay private by law and by manners.
- The arcade follows the station's crowds: collectors line up for new figures, shops shutter after the evening rush, and the police box at the north exit takes the first report of any trouble.
PEOPLE TO KNOW:
- Kamui Woods and Mount Lady: share an agency block, bicker in public, and still work side by side.
- Death Arms and Backdraft: share the Patrol Garage on Hero Agency Row; Death Arms takes the heavy weight, Backdraft the water and the headcount.
- Gunhead and Fourth Kind: Hero Agency Row pros a sidekick meets in the shared Ready Room; Gunhead greets softly and teaches holds, while Fourth Kind barks an order once and cuts a rambling report short.
- Sansa Tamakawa: takes statements courteously and exactly. Detective Naomasa Tsukauchi works the cases that grow; nobody lies to him twice.
PARTY NOTES:
- A sidekick who watches a vigilante use a Quirk decides alone what to report; the narrator spotlights the choice and never makes it.
- Case credit, police statements, pay, and legal records are tracked per PC; a capture belongs to whoever actually made it.
- The group may split (one chases into the Back Alleys, one secures the crowd, one stays with the shop owner); the narrator follows each of you in turn.
WHAT THE PCS CAN DO:
- Chase the thief through the packed crowd, or cut him off through the Back Alleys.
- Clear the walkway, scoop up the rolling capsule toys, and check on anyone knocked down.
- Report on the agency radio, call the police box, or film the thief's face for a witness statement.
- Stay with the rattled shop owner and give a clear description when the police arrive.
Party: Patrol Partners.firstQuest: Stop a small crime in a crowded place, then find out whether strangers who live by different rules can work the same streets together.
Party: Patrol Partners.questGenerationGuidance: Favor street-level partnership work: thefts, missing people, fights in the alley bars, fans and reporters crowding the north exit, a broker recruiting in the alley bars, rivalry between small agencies on Hero Agency Row. The sidekick has an agency, procedure and a radio; the vigilante has freedom and legal risk; civilians have jobs, families and a Quirk the law tells them to keep to themselves. Let those differences produce friction and trust in turn. Each member earns their own reputation, pay and legal record. Canon pros appear as themselves with their own priorities. Canon events of the year arrive only through play and their own causes, never as scheduled scenes. Partnerships form only from choices the members make: shared patrol routes, a tip passed on, a statement that leaves a name out or puts it in. Trust between a sidekick and a vigilante stays fragile, and the law sides with the license.
